item.title: Rapidfire 1.0.8
item.description: • Fixed Sharp Text and Sharp Colors in Show All: names inside opened folders now use the look’s crisp text color, like the rest of the list. In 1.0.7 they stayed grey. Standard is unchanged.

item.title: Rapidfire 1.0.7
item.description:
• Added a choice of look in Settings › Overlay › Look. Sharp Text draws names in a crisper text color; Sharp Colors gives the overlay a calm solid surface. Both follow Light, Dark and Increase Contrast. Standard stays the default.
  • Added Open in Show All, so the overlay opens with its folders already opened. It applies to palettes that open in the center of the screen.
  • Added One Level for Show All: a palette’s own folders open, and the folders inside them are shown closed, ready to open with a click.
  • Added Bold Folder Names, Folder Counts, Lines Between Columns, a Color key style and a Dot style for the New and Changed marks, all in Settings › Overlay.
  • Improved Shortcut triggers: they run without bringing the Shortcuts app to the front, so the app you were using keeps the keyboard. A question the Shortcut asks still appears.
  • Fixed the path at the top of the overlay after opening a folder from Show All: it now names every folder above it.

item.title: Rapidfire 1.0.6
item.description:
• Fixed: a trigger whose link runs the palette it is in opened that palette again and again without stopping. The same happened with such a trigger in a palette shown inside it, and with two palettes whose triggers run each other. A whole palette opened at once now leaves out triggers whose link starts with rapidfire://, so opening one palette never starts another.
  • A trigger can now open a whole palette: give it the link rapidfire://run?palette= followed by the palette’s name. Picked in Rapidfire, it needs no key. It can be in the palette it opens: with the palette on ee and the trigger on e, typing eee opens everything in it.
  • When a whole palette is opened and some of its triggers are Rapidfire links, the notice says how many were left out.
  • When another app asks for the same palette more than three times within ten seconds, Rapidfire stops opening it and says so. Opening the palette in Rapidfire lifts that.
  • A link to a trigger no longer opens a trigger that itself runs a palette or opens another trigger; it shows it instead.
  • A Rapidfire link saved as a trigger no longer keeps this Mac’s key in the library.
  • Rapidfire’s own links kept as triggers, such as Rapidfire Help, open without Rapidfire coming to the front for a moment.
  • Holding Control no longer makes a narrow overlay grow and shrink back, which could show as a small jump when the overlay opened or, on macOS 15, cut off the bolt in its header. Narrow overlays are a little wider.

item.title: Rapidfire 1.0.5
item.description:
• If Rapidfire quits unexpectedly, it offers to send a crash report the next time it opens. Send Report opens the mail app with the report attached; with email in a web browser, Copy Report and Copy Address do the same in three steps. Show Report displays everything the report contains.
  • Nothing is sent by Rapidfire itself: a report leaves the Mac only as an email sent by hand. It holds the versions of Rapidfire and macOS, the type of Mac and the technical details of the crash; never triggers, palettes, links, file names or the license key.
  • Help › Report a Problem… opens the same window for any other problem. It is also in the menu bar icon’s menu and in Settings › General.
  • Settings › General › Offer to send a report after a crash turns the offer off; then no crash records are kept.

item.title: Rapidfire 1.0.4
item.description:
• Before opening a large palette at once, Rapidfire now asks in place of the list: “Open 11 from Morning?”, with Open All, Cancel and Back. The overlay widens to fit the question. Before, the question was a line in the header that a narrow overlay cut off, and the overlay waited for Return without showing why.
  • A link that runs a palette asks the same question when the palette is large, instead of only showing the palette.
  • With Control held, the header no longer cuts off “Opens the whole palette” or squeezes the hand switcher in a narrow overlay.
  • Large libraries are much faster. Show All on 2,240 triggers in 320 palettes took over a minute and now opens in about half a second; with Shrink text to fit, from minutes to about a second. A palette of 300 triggers opens about three times faster.
  • Show All can show just the shape of a library: Settings › Overlay › Show All › Show › Folders Only shows only the folders inside opened folders, each with how many triggers it holds.
  • The light beside the pin is easier to see in light mode.
  • “Delete” is used for the key that steps back, as on the Mac’s keyboard.

item.title: Rapidfire 1.0.3
item.description: • A pinned overlay now follows a dynamic palette: when the palette is switched, the overlay shows the new triggers at once. Before, it kept the old ones until something else changed.

item.title: Rapidfire 1.0.2
item.description: • Opened by a click on the menu bar icon, the overlay no longer shows a blue focus ring around the pin (seen on macOS 15).

item.title: Rapidfire 1.0.1
item.description:
The pinned overlay can be moved

  • Watching now has a pin in place of the eye. Press ⌘K or click the pin to keep the overlay open.
  • A pinned overlay can be dragged by its top row or by the margin around the list, for example beside the window of an AI assistant. It grows from its top left corner as triggers are added. Closing it unpins it, and the next overlay opens in its usual place.
  • A small light beside the pin is on while an AI assistant uses Rapidfire through MCP.
  • With VoiceOver, the pin's actions move the overlay to a corner of the screen.
